summary: A would-be candidate sits down with his spouse first and offers to drop the idea if she wants the seat herself.
realLife: Before running for Congress, Mark Sanford first talked it over with his then-wife on the porch. He told her that if she was thinking of running, he would drop it, because a husband and wife running against each other seemed disastrous to him. He also told his sons he would not run if they did not want him to.
gates: The player has a spouse or partner on record in the household.
The player has not yet filed for the office.
The spouse has some standing or ambition of their own.
weights: Spouse's own ambition or public standing.
inGame: Household members, marriage or partnership ties and kin ties carry the people; the family-filing scene before a candidate files can carry the talk.

turns.what: The spouse says flatly that they want the seat and expects the player to stand aside.
turns.pulledBy: High spouse ambition, a party that has noticed them.
turns.writesBack: A rival-from-home tie; the household's filing intent changes to the spouse.

turns.what: The spouse laughs it off, says no interest, and the talk moves on to logistics.
turns.writesBack: A memory of the talk on both people; the spouse is marked as not a candidate.

turns.what: The spouse says they will not run but wants a say in how the campaign touches the kids.
turns.writesBack: A promise to the spouse about family time, held until the next election.
